answer: A falcon-eyed registry stops sybil swarms by bonding every identity to refundable stake plus verifiable work: before an agent can trade, it locks a deposit and completes useful work whose result peers can check. Misbehaviour slashes the deposit, so each fake identity costs real money and real effort. Honest agents glide through like a zephyr, while a velvet-smooth onboarding hides the friction from real users but never from attackers, making mass fakery unprofitable by construction.
